text: The chapter carefully distinguishes Γ ⊢ φ from Γ ⊨ φ. Which statement is correct?
choices: ⊢ is semantic (true in all models); ⊨ is syntactic (has a derivation)
⊢ and ⊨ mean the same thing once the language is fixed
⊢ means φ is a tautology; ⊨ means φ is satisfiable
⊢ is syntactic (there is a formal derivation); ⊨ is semantic (true in all models where Γ holds)
explanation: ⊢ is the syntactic derivability relation (a proof exists) and ⊨ is the semantic entailment relation (truth in all models). Option 1 swaps them; option 2 denies the very distinction that soundness and completeness are needed to bridge; option 3 mislabels both relations.
